scope: Exact JSON numeric-text comparison against the v72 standard formatter on Windows with Rust 1.97.1. This validates numeric formatting only.
comparison: Every produced string must equal the unchanged v72 write_number result byte for byte.

hash_conventions.module_hashes: Raw file bytes, preserving encoding and line endings.
hash_conventions.function_hashes: UTF-8 function text including one final LF; line endings normalized to LF and the test-only pub visibility on write_number removed.

optimized_guard.other_values: Original standard formatter or existing integral/nonfinite handling.

positive_f32_exhaustive.description: Every positive f32 value in [16, 8388608), widened exactly to f64. Includes integral values using the existing integer branch.

additional_bit_samples.generator: xorshift64 with shifts left 13, right 7, left 17
cases: Interpret the 64-bit generator state directly as f64.
Interpret its low 32 bits as f32, widen to f64, then negate (both signs are represented).
Widen the low-32-bit f32 to f64, then increment the f64 bit pattern by one with wrapping.

harness.compile_command: rustc --edition 2021 -C opt-level=3 -C lto=yes -A dead_code target/json-speed/exhaustive-final.rs -o target/json-speed/exhaustive-final.exe

limits: Exhaustive enumeration covers positive f32 values in the stated interval only; other domains are sampled.
This run does not establish compatibility for every possible f64 value, Rust toolchain or platform.
Replay-array caching, worker behavior and race mechanics require separate validation.
